description: MobileCapabilitiesService.getMyCapabilities returns a theme block { pairId, label, light, dark, version } alongside features
Predefined pair: light/dark token sets are taken from CUSTOM_THEME_PRESETS for the tenant's pairId
Custom pair (Enterprise): light/dark token sets are the tenant's saved custom tokens
Custom pair with tokens failing findInvalidCustomThemeTokens falls back to the Alga preset and reports pairId 'alga'
Tenant with no saved theme resolves to the default pair (alga) rather than omitting the block
theme.label is the pair's English label from THEME_PAIRS ('Custom' for custom)
theme.version is a stable hash of pairId plus both token sets (same input → same hash, any token change → new hash)
OpenAPI entry for /api/v1/mobile/me/capabilities documents the theme block and a MobileThemeSeedTokens schema with the 15 keys
ee/mobile/src/ui/themeMath.ts ports hexToRgb, mix, rampFromStops and brandRamp with the same signatures and numeric behaviour as packages/tenancy customTheme.ts
themeMath exports rgbToHex and contrastRatio (WCAG relative luminance) for textInverse selection
A committed fixture (themeMath.fixture.json) holds ramp outputs generated from the web implementation for all nine presets in both modes
ui/themeTokens.ts defines MobileThemeSeedTokens (15 keys), MobileTheme { pairId, label, light, dark, version } and a parse/guard for untrusted input
buildTheme(tokens, mode, { pairId }) returns a complete Theme with spacing, radii, shadows and typography unchanged from the current file
buildTheme maps background, card, text, textSecondary, placeholder, border and borderLight from the seed tokens and the neutral ramp per FR7
buildTheme maps primary, primaryLight, primaryDark from the primary brand ramp per FR7
buildTheme maps secondary, cyan and accent from the secondary and accent brand ramps per FR7
buildTheme picks textInverse as white when white reaches 4.5:1 on primary, otherwise textPrimary
buildTheme uses fixed per-mode status colours (danger, warning, success, info, orange, indigo) matching the web base tokens
buildTheme derives badge sets (info, success, warning, danger, neutral) by mixing each status colour with the card colour at the documented per-mode ratios
buildTheme derives toast sets (info, success, error) from the same status/card mixing
buildTheme substitutes the built-in Alga value for any individual token that fails to parse and logs once per version
lightTheme and darkTheme exports in ui/themes.ts are produced by buildTheme from the embedded Alga preset and remain the fallback
The embedded Alga preset in the app is the only palette shipped in the binary; no other pair's tokens are hard-coded
api/capabilities.ts MyCapabilities gains an optional theme field typed as MobileTheme
CapabilitiesProvider exposes theme (or null) and refreshes it on the same triggers as features (sign-in, resume, focus)
ThemeProvider builds the active theme from the capabilities theme block, memoised per (version, mode), and falls back to the Alga pair when absent
ThemeProvider caches the theme block in secure storage under alga.mobile.theme.tokens.<baseUrl>.<tenantId> whenever a new version arrives
On launch ThemeProvider reads the cached block for the current server+tenant before the first themed frame so warm launches show the tenant pair, not Alga
Signing out or changing the server host clears the cached theme block and reverts to Alga
The light/dark/system preference continues to select which half of the pair renders and keeps its existing storage key
ThemeContext exposes the active pairId and label for the Settings row
Settings gains an Appearance section with a row cycling System → Light → Dark bound to useThemePreference
Settings shows a read-only Theme row with the pair label and the hint 'Set by your administrator in AlgaPSA settings', or 'Default' when no theme was sent
settings.json gains the appearance and theme strings; no hard-coded English in the rows
DocumentsSection preview overlay uses theme tokens for its text and controls; the black scrim stays literal
ScanView chrome, SignInScreen, MentionSuggestionList and MaterialsSection replace hex literals with theme tokens
ESLint restricts hex colour literals under src/** with an allow-list for themes.ts, colors.ts, tagColors.ts, Avatar.tsx and generatedEditorHtml.ts
The generated editor HTML declares CSS variables for background, text, secondary text, link, mention background and mention text with the current light defaults
bridge.ts gains a setTheme message that updates those CSS variables at runtime
TicketRichTextEditor sends setTheme on load and whenever the active theme changes (editable and read-only)
CommentsSection, DescriptionSection and ExpandableComment render through the themed editor so comment bodies match the card
Theme carries a contrast flag derived from pairId === 'high-contrast'
Card, KeyValue and list rows use the strong border token when the contrast flag is set
Badge draws a one-pixel border in its status colour when the contrast flag is set
A mobile test builds all nine presets in both modes from the committed fixture and asserts the mapped tokens match expected values
A mobile test runs the ported contrast checks over all nine built themes and asserts no failures
A server test pins the theme block for each predefined pair to CUSTOM_THEME_PRESETS and asserts the custom fallback path
Device pass checklist in SCRATCHPAD.md completed for Alga, Forest, Vice, High contrast and one custom pair, light and dark
